summary: At just half a square mile, Mayfair is one of the most densely packed census-designated places in the San Joaquin Valley — over 10,000 people per square mile crammed into a flat, grid-street pocket on the eastern edge of Fresno, where the terrain is unrelentingly level and the sky stretches wide over agricultural land to the east. That density number rivals parts of San Francisco, yet the median home value sits at roughly $244,200, yielding a home-price-to-income ratio near 4.1 — genuinely attainable compared to coastal California, though a 22.2% poverty rate signals that even local housing costs press hard against actual earnings. The economy here orbits Fresno's major employers in healthcare, agriculture, logistics, and public-sector roles, meaning most working residents commute outward rather than finding employment within Mayfair's tiny footprint. Summers are serious — average highs pushing well into the upper 80s and 90s with nearly ten hours of daily sunshine — while winters stay mild enough to keep outdoor errands comfortable year-round. The area's character is shaped by its position: absorbed into Fresno's urban fabric but technically unincorporated, it functions less as a standalone community and more as a high-density residential node whose identity is inseparable from the larger city surrounding it.
